content.text:
Prompt Interpretation: You want me to research and compile evidence that Keir Starmer values human rights, using current, credible sources. For each source I use, you want the link, a short summary, and my trust assessment with reasoning. You also asked to see my step-by-step reasoning; I can give a concise, non-sensitive overview of my approach and assumptions, but I won’t disclose my hidden chain-of-thought. I will then provide a documented conclusion.

Reasoning Process: 
- Define the claim: “values human rights” = consistent public commitments, concrete actions in office, and a prior professional record aligned with international human rights norms (e.g., UDHR, ECHR).
- Gather sources: prioritise primary/official materials (GOV.UK transcripts, party policy), reputable news (Reuters/Politico/Irish Times/FT), and authoritative biographies or publishers (Britannica, Routledge). Include legal-career evidence (death penalty litigation; policing human-rights oversight).
- Cross-check and date-stamp key items: ensure statements/actions are dated and recent (notably 2024–2025).
- Evaluate trust: rate each source (TRUSTED/NOT TRUSTED/Trusted with caveats) and explain why.
- Synthesize: weigh the legal-career record + explicit ECHR commitments + policy choices (ending Rwanda scheme) to reach a balanced conclusion. 

Assumptions:
- “Prove” is treated as “present strong, sourced evidence.” In politics, absolute proof is unattainable; I’m providing best-available evidence from high-quality sources.
- Valuing human rights does not mean never balancing them with other policy aims; statements about reviewing interpretation of laws (not withdrawal) can be consistent with human-rights commitment.
- You are in the UK; dates below are in day-month-year or ISO format and refer to the cited items as published.

Final Answer:
- URL: https://www.gov.uk/government/news/pm-united-nations-general-assembly-speech-26-september-2024
  - Summary: In his 26 Sep 2024 UNGA speech, Starmer says the Universal Declaration of Human Rights had a profound impact on him; he spent his legal career protecting those rights and remains inspired by them as Prime Minister.
  - Trust: TRUSTED
  - Reasoning: Official government transcript; primary source for Starmer’s words. ([gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/government/news/pm-united-nations-general-assembly-speech-26-september-2024?utm_source=openai))

- URL: https://www.politico.eu/article/britain-keir-starmer-never-leave-european-convention-human-rights-political-community-summit/
  - Summary: On 18 Jul 2024, Starmer vowed the UK would “never” leave the European Convention on Human Rights (ECHR), linking migration policy to “humanity” and “profound respect for international law.”
  - Trust: TRUSTED
  - Reasoning: Reputable outlet quoting on-the-record remarks; corroborates official stance on ECHR. ([politico.eu](https://www.politico.eu/article/britain-keir-starmer-never-leave-european-convention-human-rights-political-community-summit/?utm_source=openai))

- URL: https://labour.org.uk/change/britain-reconnected/
  - Summary: Labour’s policy page states: “Britain will unequivocally remain a member of the European Convention on Human Rights,” and commits to upholding human rights and international law.
  - Trust: TRUSTED
  - Reasoning: Official party position; authoritative for Starmer government policy. ([labour.org.uk](https://labour.org.uk/change/britain-reconnected/?utm_source=openai))

- URL: https://www.standard.co.uk/news/politics/keir-starmer-shabana-mahmood-government-prime-minister-liberal-democrat-b1245793.html
  - Summary: During PMQs on 3 Sep 2025, Starmer said leaving the ECHR would be a “profound mistake” and “catastrophic,” while rejecting any withdrawal or suspension.
  - Trust: TRUSTED
  - Reasoning: UK news piece based on PA reporting and direct Commons exchanges; aligns with multiple reports. ([standard.co.uk](https://www.standard.co.uk/news/politics/keir-starmer-shabana-mahmood-government-prime-minister-liberal-democrat-b1245793.html?utm_source=openai))

- URL: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/asylum-claims-under-the-migration-and-economic-development-partnership
  - Summary: Home Office guidance notes that in July 2024 the government discontinued the previous policy to remove certain asylum seekers to Rwanda.
  - Trust: TRUSTED
  - Reasoning: Official policy update; primary source confirming the scrapping of a policy widely criticised on human-rights grounds. ([gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/asylum-claims-under-the-migration-and-economic-development-partnership?utm_source=openai))

- URL: https://www.gov.uk/government/speeches/pm-remarks-at-the-organised-immigration-summit-in-central-london-31-march-2025
  - Summary: On 31 Mar 2025 Starmer said resources were being redeployed away from the “wasteful Rwanda scheme,” emphasising lawful returns and system fixes instead of gimmicks.
  - Trust: TRUSTED
  - Reasoning: Official PM remarks confirming the operational end and rationale; complements the policy update above. ([gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/government/speeches/pm-remarks-at-the-organised-immigration-summit-in-central-london-31-march-2025?utm_source=openai))

- URL: https://www.britannica.com/biography/Keir-Starmer
  - Summary: Biography highlights Starmer’s legal career with emphasis on human rights work, including death penalty cases and advisory roles.
  - Trust: TRUSTED
  - Reasoning: Encyclopaedia Britannica; editorially reviewed, high-quality reference. ([britannica.com](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Keir-Starmer?utm_source=openai))

- URL: https://www.routledge.com/The-Three-Pillars-of-Liberty-Political-Rights-and-Freedoms-in-the-Unit/Klug-Starmer-Weir/p/book/9780415096416
  - Summary: Starmer co-authored a 1996 landmark audit of UK compliance with international human rights standards (The Three Pillars of Liberty).
  - Trust: TRUSTED
  - Reasoning: Publisher page evidences long-standing scholarly engagement with human rights. ([routledge.com](https://www.routledge.com/The-Three-Pillars-of-Liberty-Political-Rights-and-Freedoms-in-the-Unit/Klug-Starmer-Weir/p/book/9780415096416?utm_source=openai))

- URL: https://deathpenaltyproject.org/privy-council-abolishes-mandatory-death-penalty-in-the-bahamas/
  - Summary: Following a Privy Council ruling abolishing the mandatory death penalty in The Bahamas (2006), Keir Starmer QC hailed it as “a new dawn for human rights in the region.”
  - Trust: TRUSTED
  - Reasoning: Specialist legal NGO with case documentation; includes Starmer’s contemporaneous quote. ([deathpenaltyproject.org](https://deathpenaltyproject.org/privy-council-abolishes-mandatory-death-penalty-in-the-bahamas/?utm_source=openai))

- URL: https://cain.ulster.ac.uk/issues/police/source.htm
  - Summary: University of Ulster’s CAIN archive lists “A Report on the Policing of the Ardoyne Parades, 12 July 2004” authored by Keir Starmer and Jane Gordon for the Northern Ireland Policing Board.
  - Trust: TRUSTED
  - Reasoning: Academic archive indexing the report; corroborates his human-rights oversight work in policing. ([cain.ulster.ac.uk](https://cain.ulster.ac.uk/issues/police/source.htm?utm_source=openai))

- URL: https://www.irishtimes.com/news/psni-cleared-over-tactics-at-parade-in-ardoyne-1.1165022
  - Summary: News report (5 Nov 2004) notes human-rights experts Keir Starmer QC and Jane Gordon assessed PSNI conduct at a contentious parade, finding compliance with human rights.
  - Trust: TRUSTED
  - Reasoning: Reputable newspaper contemporaneous reporting; confirms authors’ human-rights assessment role. ([irishtimes.com](https://www.irishtimes.com/news/psni-cleared-over-tactics-at-parade-in-ardoyne-1.1165022?utm_source=openai))

- URL: https://www.gov.uk/government/speeches/prime-ministers-statement-at-the-un-security-council
  - Summary: At the UN Security Council (25 Sep 2024), Starmer emphasised humanitarian principles, tribute to aid workers, and the Council’s duty to protect peace and security.
  - Trust: TRUSTED
  - Reasoning: Official transcript; supports consistency in international-law/human-rights framing. ([gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/government/speeches/prime-ministers-statement-at-the-un-security-council?utm_source=openai))

- URL: https://www.ft.com/content/e0dd36ed-c692-4e6e-a663-350eedf83768
  - Summary: Late Sep/early Oct 2025 reporting that Starmer wants to “look again” at the interpretation of some ECHR provisions for migration cases—while not dismantling the framework.
  - Trust: TRUSTED
  - Reasoning: Financial Times; careful reporting on legal-policy nuance consistent with staying in the ECHR. ([ft.com](https://www.ft.com/content/e0dd36ed-c692-4e6e-a663-350eedf83768?utm_source=openai))

- URL: https://www.amnesty.org.uk/over-13000-people-took-action-calling-prime-minister-prioritise-human-rights
  - Summary: Amnesty UK notes Starmer has said human rights will be central to government work and urges him to deliver on that promise (with a 2023 quote).
  - Trust: TRUSTED (with caveat)
  - Reasoning: Advocacy group; not neutral on policy, but accurately cites and compiles relevant statements; use as supporting, not sole, evidence. ([amnesty.org.uk](https://www.amnesty.org.uk/over-13000-people-took-action-calling-prime-minister-prioritise-human-rights?utm_source=openai))

- URL: https://labour.org.uk/change/scotland-a-strong-and-connected-country/
  - Summary: Reiterates that under Labour “the UK will unequivocally remain” in the ECHR as part of security and international-law commitments.
  - Trust: TRUSTED
  - Reasoning: Official party text; corroborates ECHR commitment across regional pages. ([labour.org.uk](https://labour.org.uk/change/scotland-a-strong-and-connected-country/?utm_source=openai))

Conclusion:
- Across decades, Starmer’s actions and record align with valuing human rights:
  - Legal career: extensive human-rights litigation and scholarship (death penalty challenges, human-rights policing oversight, authorship of a major human-rights audit). ([deathpenaltyproject.org](https://deathpenaltyproject.org/privy-council-abolishes-mandatory-death-penalty-in-the-bahamas/?utm_source=openai))
  - Explicit commitments in office: multiple, dated statements to keep the UK in the ECHR and to root policy in international law. ([politico.eu](https://www.politico.eu/article/britain-keir-starmer-never-leave-european-convention-human-rights-political-community-summit/?utm_source=openai))
  - Policy choices: discontinuation of the Rwanda removals scheme and reallocation of resources, consistent with a more rights-compliant approach, even while seeking stricter interpretations in specific migration contexts. ([gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/asylum-claims-under-the-migration-and-economic-development-partnership?utm_source=openai))

Given these converging strands of evidence, it is reasonable to conclude that Keir Starmer does value human rights as a core principle, reflected in his professional background, stated positions, and key policy decisions.
